text:
The nymph Flora wept for shepherd Menalcas,
for the strange and grievous, cruel event;
and from her lovely face—alas, hard fate!—
the roses darkened and lost their color.

Now she makes herself weep, then turns and weeps,
turning her tears to great pearls;
now she lies dead and cold, and if death
lets her breathe, she sometimes says:

“Fate, if you fell in love with my beloved,
cut the uncertain thread of my life;
you shall enjoy your power, I my deception.

But, ah, what am I saying? You did not miss:
in killing him, you killed me too;
you struck him, yet I feel the wound.”

translation.title: To a Lady Weeping for Her Dead Servant
